windstormCounty.note: Galveston County is a whole-county TDI designated catastrophe area; League City is listed as Inland I. The Inland I/II line in Galveston County follows the Brazoria/Galveston county line north from SH 6 to Friendswood's southern limits, then Friendswood's eastern limits to the Harris County line - it is NOT tied to I-45, so all of League City (Galveston part) is Inland I. A small part of League City lies in Harris County (Harris designation covers only La Porte/Seabrook/Shoreacres/Morgan's Point/Pasadena east of SH 146) - verify those parcels. source.title: League City Council agenda/video - public hearing & action amending Ch. 22 Building to adopt 2021 I-codes with local amendments

plainLanguage: League City uses the 2021 International Residential and Energy codes for city permits. Every new house in the Galveston County part of the city is in the state's 'Inland I' windstorm zone, so you also need a Texas Department of Insurance windstorm certificate (WPI-8), checked against the 2024 IRC. The usual single-family zone is RSF-7: lots of at least 7,000 sq ft and a 25-ft front setback; side and rear setbacks still need to be confirmed, and many neighborhoods are PUDs with their own plat lines. Since 2018 the city requires new homes to sit at least 24 inches above the 100-year flood level or 3 inches above the 500-year level. The building permit is about $0.40 per square foot (roughly $1,100 for a 2,400 sq ft house with garage), but water and sewer impact fees are much larger - about $11,900 to $14,800 per home since December 2023, unless your lot is in a MUD.
